scenario: [LTIM.1.1.1] utc_ns is NANOSECONDS — high half of the discriminating pair. Identical to LTIM.1.1.1_ns_boundary_alive except for the last two steps: after 1000 ns the clock advances ONE further nanosecond, landing exactly on the `1001_ns` deadline, and the fact is retracted ([LFAC.1.2], expiry at now >= deadline). Two things here are individually unrepresentable at microsecond resolution and must BOTH survive for this to pass — the 1.001 µs TTL literal, and the final 1 ns advance. The advance is a separate step deliberately: one advance of 1001 ns reaches the same instant, and a fixture that only ever moves the clock in one jump cannot tell a nanosecond clock from one that rounds the jump.
